11.zh: 打赌输了后，妹妹只好不情愿地帮我做家务。
11.note: 应选（3）'grudgingly'：义为'不情愿地'，与打赌输了不得不做家务一致。'warily'：义为'谨慎地'。'earnestly'：义为'认真地、诚恳地'，不含勉强。'deliberately'：义为'故意地'。更细的英语措辞与例证见上栏'说明'及选项表。
11.concept: 词汇辨析 — grudgingly（不情愿地）

choices.eg: She warily opened the basement door, unsure whether anyone was hiding inside.
He earnestly apologised to his coach for arriving late to every practice.
After losing our bet, my sister had no choice but to do my chores grudgingly.
He deliberately left his muddy boots on the clean carpet to annoy his sister.

12.zh: 乔治闯进来打断我们，谈话戛然而止。
12.note: 应选（1）'abrupt'：义为'突然的'，与 burst in 打断谈话一致。'eventful'：义为'多事的'。'unrealistic'：义为'不现实的'，不能修饰 end。'astounding'：义为'令人震惊的'，偏惊人而非戛然而止。更细的英语措辞与例证见上栏'说明'及选项表。
12.concept: 词汇辨析 — abrupt（突然的；突兀的）

choices.eg: Our conversation came to an abrupt end when George burst in and interrupted us.
It was an eventful day that began with a fire drill and ended with a class award.
Expecting to finish the whole project in one hour is completely unrealistic.
The magician's astounding trick left the audience speechless for several seconds.

13.zh: 老师尽责之外还常留下来辅导我们。
13.note: 应选（1）'call'：固定搭配 call of duty（职责；使命）。'tour'：义为'巡回、旅行'。'time'：义为'时间'，不能构成 call of duty。'care'：义为'关心'，常见 take care of，非本搭配。更细的英语措辞与例证见上栏'说明'及选项表。
13.concept: 词汇辨析 — call（召唤；职责）

choices.eg: My teacher goes beyond her call of duty and often stays back with us to help us with our work.
The band went on a six-month world tour after their album became a hit.
During the holidays, the children spent most of their free time reading at the library.
Please take good care of your younger brother while we are away.

14.zh: 要想团队合作，我们得搁置分歧，专心手头任务。
14.note: 应选（4）'put aside'：义为'搁置、抛开'分歧。'put in'：义为'投入（时间、努力）'。'put off'：义为'推迟'。'put down'：义为'放下'或'贬低'。更细的英语措辞与例证见上栏'说明'及选项表。
14.concept: 词汇辨析 — put aside（搁置；抛开）

choices.eg: She put in many hours of practice before the piano competition.
Heavy rain put off the school sports day until the following week.
Please put down your phones and listen to the safety briefing.
If we want to work well as a team, we need to put aside our differences and focus on the task at hand.

15.zh: 我力不从心，只好请同学帮忙完成项目。
15.note: 应选（1）'enlisted'：enlist someone's help 寻求某人帮助。'enrolled'：义为'注册入学/课程'。'mustered'：义为'召集、鼓起'，搭配 courage/support。'volunteered'：义为'自愿做'，主语是主动提供，非'去求帮'。更细的英语措辞与例证见上栏'说明'及选项表。

choices.eg: Having bitten off more than I could chew, I enlisted the help of my classmates to complete the project.
She enrolled in an online coding course during the June holidays.
The captain mustered enough courage to speak in front of the large crowd.

cloze: Along Beach Road resides one of Singapore's oldest heritage sites. It is a [Q16 (quaint)] little mosque founded by Hajjah Fatimah binte Sulaiman, one of the earliest tradeswomen in Singapore.

Originally, there stood a house with a large [Q17 (compound)] built by Hajjah Fatimah. Seeing how huge the place was, thieves [Q18 (broke into)] her house. However, they did not find anything much of value because she did not believe in [Q19 (hoarding)] material possessions. Frustrated, the thieves burnt her house down.

Luckily, Hajjah Fatimah was away on business and thus, was not harmed. Grateful that she had escaped unscathed, she donated her land as well as the funds needed for the construction of a mosque and several houses for the poor. Her [Q20 (generous)] gesture was much appreciated by the community.
Today, there are annual feasts held at the mosque in her memory.
zh: 沿着海滩路坐落着新加坡最古老的遗产之一：一座由早期女商人哈贾·法蒂玛创办的古雅小清真寺。
原先她建了一座带大院子的房子。小偷闯入，因她不囤积财物而几乎一无所获，恼怒之下烧了房子。
哈贾·法蒂玛外出经商未受伤，感恩之余捐地建清真寺并资助穷人住房，慷慨之举深受社区感激。
如今清真寺每年为她举办纪念宴会。

cloze: The essential thing in life is not conquering but fighting well! Of all the great sporting festivals held all [Q29] the world and throughout history, the Olympic Games reign supreme. They are watched by more people than any [Q30] televised event.

The Olympic Games remain as one of the few sporting competitions [Q31] the athletes do not receive any cash prizes from winning the competitions. [Q32], the glory of being an Olympic champion and receiving a gold medal is everything. After years of personal sacrifice, extreme dedication [Q33] having to train for long hours in all weather conditions, the world's greatest athletes meet every four years [Q34] decide who will be the Olympic champions. Competitors dream of standing [Q35] the winner's podium and receiving gold medals [Q36] their national anthem is being played. This is the climax of their athletic careers.

Of all the Olympic sports, the [Q37] popular are the track events. A number of sprinters, hurdlers and distance runners [Q38] become household names. It takes a lot of hard work and perseverance to reach Olympic excellence. The Olympic Games is without a doubt the most prestigious competition an athlete can take part in.
zh: 人生要义不在征服而在拼搏！奥运会是全球最伟大的体育盛会，收视超过任何其他电视赛事。
奥运是少数不设现金奖金的大赛之一；取而代之，冠军荣耀与金牌就是一切。经年牺牲与刻苦训练后，顶尖选手四年一会角逐冠军，梦想站上领奖台、国歌奏响。
田径最受欢迎，许多短跑、跨栏、长跑选手家喻户晓。奥运是运动员能参加的最负盛名的比赛。

29.note: great sporting festivals held all over the world and throughout history, = 看前后搭配，选 over。

30.note: by more people than any other televised event. = 结合句意选 other。

31.note: of the few sporting competitions where the athletes do not receive = 定语/名词性从句 → where。

32.note: instead , the glory of being = 结合句意选 instead。

33.note: of personal sacrifice, extreme dedication and having to train for long = 句间逻辑 → and。

35.note: Competitors dream of standing atop the winner's podium and receiving = 看前后搭配，选 atop。

37.note: all the Olympic sports, the most popular are the track events. = 结合句意选 most。

38.note: sprinters, hurdlers and distance runners even become household names. = 结合句意选 even。

cloze: How do we reduce food waste? When housewife Jenny Tan cooks soup for her family, she does not let the [Q39(ingreedeints)] go to waste. Instead of [Q40(discarded)] the chicken breast meat used for boiling the soup, she saves it for another dish the next day.
The 44-year-old says, "I was [Q41(bring)] up in a family where the awareness of reducing food wastage was [Q42(inculkated)] at a young age."

Keeping a food journal allows her to understand her family's daily [Q43(dieteri)] needs. She initially used it to keep track of the harvest [Q44(for)] her edible garden and to understand how the vegetables [Q45(kontribiuted)] to her daily meals. The diary helped her to plan her meals, [Q46(managing)] her food stock at home and not buy too much food.

She saves [Q47(pearishable)] food such as mangoes, blueberries and tomatoes from the bin by blending them into a puree and freezing them in ice-cube trays. She [Q48(packed)] the frozen cubes into resealable freezer-friendly bags. To help her identify the bags, she labels and dates [Q49(it)] . She usually uses the frozen fruit for smoothies.
She says, "It takes [Q50(desipline)] to reduce food wastage. But ultimately I save money."
zh: 如何减少食物浪费？主妇陈珍妮煮汤时不浪费食材，煮汤的鸡胸肉留作次日另一道菜。
四十四岁的她说，自己成长于重视减少浪费的家庭，这种意识从小被灌输。
饮食日记帮她了解家人每日膳食需求，记录菜园收成与蔬菜如何贡献餐桌，从而规划餐食、管理库存。
她把芒果、蓝莓、番茄等易腐食物打成泥冻成冰块，再装入可密封冷冻袋并贴标签日期，用来做冰沙。
她说，减少浪费需要自律，但最终能省钱。

cloze: Bees and wasps are two insects that are closely related. They both play [Q51] important role in nature as pollinators, transferring pollen as they travel from plant to plant. Without them, plants cannot thrive, and we may not have beautiful blooming flowers to [Q52] at. These insects are crucial to farming. Because of them, crops can flourish. Otherwise, there might be a shortage [Q53] food such as fruit, rice or wheat.

[Q54] from helping to cross-fertilise plants, wasps kill many pests like caterpillars. These pests destroy crops. As their population can quickly grow out of [Q55], they can bring much harm to crops. When wasps kill pests, they help to [Q56] their numbers in check. It is a well-known fact that bees make honey, [Q57] is often sold in supermarkets as a superfood. Honey is also used in skincare and in many home remedies to fight ailments. Thus, bees are considered by many as useful insects.

Both bees and wasps live in colonies. The queen is an important member of the colony as it enjoys a higher rank [Q58] other members. Usually, there is only one queen in each colony but paper wasps, [Q59] example, have more than one queen. The queens are not equal in rank and paper wasps [Q60] the ability to recognise their different faces.
While people generally are accepting of bees, the same [Q61] be said of wasps. In cartoons and songs, the former are often portrayed as adorable and hardworking.

However, the [Q62] are one of those insects that many love to hate. People find wasps annoying [Q63] to a lack of awareness amongst the public about the usefulness of wasps. Many people only know wasps as dangerous insects that sting, to be avoided [Q64] all costs.
Wasps badly need a [Q65] in public opinion. Hopefully, with education, people will come to view wasps favourably as much as bees.
zh: 蜜蜂和黄蜂是两种亲缘关系密切的昆虫。它们在自然界中都作为传粉者发挥着重要作用，在植物间穿梭时传播花粉。没有它们，植物就无法蓬勃生长，我们可能也就没有美丽的繁花可以欣赏。这些昆虫对农业至关重要。有了它们，农作物才能茁壮成长。否则，水果、大米或小麦等食物可能会出现短缺。
除了帮助植物异花授粉外，黄蜂还会杀死许多像毛毛虫这样的害虫。这些害虫会破坏庄稼。由于害虫的数量会迅速失控，它们会给农作物带来很大危害。当黄蜂杀死害虫时，它们有助于将害虫数量控制在合理范围内。众所周知，蜜蜂酿造蜂蜜，蜂蜜常作为超级食物在超市出售。蜂蜜还被用于护肤和许多治疗疾病的家庭偏方中。因此，许多人认为蜜蜂是有益的昆虫。
蜜蜂和黄蜂都过着群居生活。蜂后是群体中的重要成员，因为它的等级高于其他成员。通常每个群体只有一只蜂后，但以纸蜂为例，它们拥有不止一只蜂后。这些蜂后的等级并不平等，而且纸蜂具有辨认不同面孔的能力。
虽然人们普遍接受蜜蜂，但对黄蜂却不能这么说。在动画片和歌曲中，前者通常被描绘成可爱且勤劳的形象。
然而，后者（黄蜂）却是许多人深恶痛绝的昆虫之一。人们觉得黄蜂讨厌，是因为公众对黄蜂的益处缺乏认识。许多人只知道黄蜂是会蜇人的危险昆虫，必须不惜一切代价避开。
黄蜂极需改善公众舆论对它的看法。希望通过教育，人们会像喜爱蜜蜂一样对黄蜂产生好感。

51.note: 修饰以元音音素开头的单数可数名词短语 important role。在描述两类昆虫所扮演的自然角色的特定语境下，完美契合极高频经典搭配 play an important role，意为它们在自然界中“起着重要作用”。

52.note: 作为定语修饰成分，后接专属介词 at。描述观赏盛开鲜花的场景，指我们可能无法拥有美丽的鲜花来供人们“观赏”、“凝视”或“惊叹”，故填入动词原形 look / gaze / marvel / stare（此处 look 最符合基础大纲规范）。

53.note: 连接前面的名词 shortage 和后面的名词短语 food such as...。在探讨粮食短缺的农业科普场景下，完美契合高频核心专属搭配 a shortage of something，意为可能会引发食物“短缺”。

54.note: 后接介词短语 from helping to cross-fertilise plants。前文提到了传粉，此处引导逻辑递进。填入 Apart 或 Aside 构成 Apart from / Aside from 结构，表示“除了”协助植物异花授粉之外，胡蜂还能消灭害虫。位于句首需大写。

55.note: 与前置的动词短语 grow out of 完美组合。在描述害虫种群数量失去管教的灾难场景下，构成高频标志性专属局势失控习语 grow out of hand（或者是表示由于失去控制而失控的 control / check / bound，此处原答案表锁定的 hand 最地道常见），意为数量会“迅速失控/失去控制”。

56.concept: 动词与宾语及介词短语特定搭配
56.note: 动词不定式符号 help to... 后接动词原形。与后面的名词宾语 their numbers 极其介词短语 in check 完美组合，构成在各类环境、公共卫生议题里高频重复考核的核心地道专属搭配 keep something in check，意为帮助将害虫数量“控制在一定范围内”。

57.concept: 非限制性定语从句关系代词
57.note: 引导非限制性定语从句，修饰代指非人、物及食品概念的单数先行词 honey（蜂蜜）。从句中缺少主语成分，且指代物，故固定填入关系代词 which（在非限制性定语从句中不能用 that 替代）。

58.note: 前文出现了明确的形容词比较级限制词 higher rank。与之呼应并构成社群内部等级地位对比的必然是比较连词 than，用来指代蜂王享有的级别“高于”其他普通成员。

59.concept: 举例说明固定习惯搭配
59.note: 与前置的名词短语 paper wasps 极其后置的名词 instance 完美组合，用作两个逗号之间的插入语。完美契合最经典的高频例证引导习语 for example 或者是 for instance（例如）。

60.note: 主语为复数名词 paper wasps（马蜂），陈述客观存在的生物学事实，谓语动词用原形。指这类马蜂“拥有（have/possess）”辨认不同面孔的惊人能力，后接名词宾语 the ability。

61.concept: 情态动词绝对否定句型形式
61.note: 主语为单数名词短语 the same，后接被动语态短语 be said of wasps。完美契合英语中用于表示此消彼长、截然相反评价的极高频标志性专属对照比喻句式 the same cannot/can't be said for/of someone，意为但同样的话却“不能”用在胡蜂身上（因为人们讨厌胡蜂）。

62.concept: 篇章指代对照限定名词
62.note: 由定冠词 The 引导修饰。前文刚刚提到了 the former（前者，指代蜜蜂），此处与之形成经典、完美的篇章对称指代，填入单复数对照代词 latter（或者是复数形式的 wasps 呼应 are），表示“后者（胡蜂）”往往是人们最讨厌的昆虫之一。由于后文谓语是 are，填入名词 wasps 亦完全通顺。位于句首需大写。

63.note: 后接名词短语 a lack of awareness。与后面的介词 to 完美组合，构成高频常考的经典原因表达 due to 或者是 owing to，用以引出因为公众缺乏对胡蜂益处的了解才导致产生厌恶情绪的因果背景。

64.note: 与其后置的代词限定结构 all costs 完美结合。构成全行业、各大名校考卷中出题率极高、用于形容采取决绝手段斩断隐患的专属比喻绝断习语 at all costs，意为人们普遍认为胡蜂是应当被“不惜一切代价”所远离的危险害虫。

65.note: 由不定冠词 a 引导，后接介词短语 in public opinion（公众舆论中）。结合后文“希望通过教育，人们未来能像看待蜜蜂那样客观地看待胡蜂”的积极展望，指胡蜂极度需要迎来一次形象上的“改观”、“转变”、“提升”或“转变”，故填名词 change / shift / turn / transformation / reversal / improvement。

lines.1: Life in Singapore in the 1930s was carefree even though war had just started raging in
lines.2: Europe. I lived with my parents in a wooden house on Ganges Road.
lines.3: I remembered the monsoon seasons when fierce rain clouds would roll in frequently.
lines.4: It poured heavily and noisily for hours during the day. At sundown, the frogs croaked from
lines.5: the wasteland. Incessant and loud, it reminded Father of his childhood days in Tao Yuan
lines.6: Chun, a village in China. His family was very poor. When he was young, Father started
lines.7: working for a farmer in the paddy fields. Months later, that farmer taught him how to catch
lines.9: "I often waded into the paddy fields to catch frogs as there were many to catch. Your
lines.10: grandmother was always happy whenever I came home with something extra for the
lines.11: cooking pot. On these occasions, all my family members cleaned their plates. Nothing was
lines.12: left," he said. He always smiled when he told me this story of his childhood. I, on the other
lines.13: hand, found the thought of touching the slimy frogs revolting.
lines.14: One day, Father decided that he was going to try and catch some frogs. He was
lines.15: planning to bring me along on my first frog hunt. It would be fun, he told me and that
lines.16: convinced me to give it a try. However, my mother was against **his idea**. I told her that I
lines.17: was already Father's age when he started catching frogs and eventually, she gave in. I told
lines.18: Father that I would bring along some butterfly nets.
lines.19: "When you spot a frog, raise the net with your hands and quickly bring it down over the
lines.20: creature," said Father, demonstrating with his net. "Stay there and don't move until I come
lines.21: and take it from underneath." I readily agreed as I really did not want to touch a frog.
lines.22: When the sun flashed its last rays, our hunt began in earnest. My heart pounded
lines.23: against my chest. The ground on the wasteland was overgrown with mimosa plants full of
lines.24: thorns. The **nasty weeds** pricked our feet from the sides as we were wearing slippers.
lines.25: It was uncomfortable to walk in them. There was also tall grass, commonly known as lalang,
lines.26: on the wasteland. Parting the lalang as we went, we were careful not to get cut by their
lines.27: sharp edges. Soon, we realised it was not easy to use the net. The lalang was far too long.
lines.28: When we brought the net down over a frog, the thick lalang bent and cushioned the net,
lines.29: leaving enough space between the grass and the ground for the frog to escape.
lines.30: We realised later that the only way was to run after them and try to seize them with our
lines.31: bare hands! I had no choice but to overcome my fear. Nervously, I crouched down to catch
lines.32: one but to no avail. The slimy creatures slipped from my hands every time and escaped
lines.33: into the holes in the ground. I was disheartened and wanted to quit but Father encouraged
lines.34: me to press on. I could not believe it when, after many tries, I finally managed to catch one.
lines.35: I whooped in delight and showed my prize to Father.
lines.36: "It's often the last key in the bunch that opens the lock!" he said, giving me a pat
lines.38: The next day, during lunch, we savoured the **fruits of our labour**. Out of the four that
lines.39: we caught, Father said that mine was the biggest. As we ate the frog porridge, I learnt that
lines.40: we should not give up when things do not go our way.

paragraphs.1: 二十世纪三十年代新加坡生活无忧无虑，尽管欧洲刚爆发战争。我与父母住在甘榜路木屋。
paragraphs.3: 每当季候风季节来临，暴雨云总是频繁袭来。白天，大雨倾盆，雷声大作，持续数小时。日落时分，荒地上的青蛙便开始聒噪。那连绵不绝的叫声让父亲想起了他在中国桃源村的童年。那时他家里很穷。父亲小小年纪就去帮农夫种稻。几个月后，农夫教会了他怎么抓青蛙。
paragraphs.9: “我经常下到稻田里抓青蛙，因为那里有很多。每当带回额外的食材下锅，祖母总是特别高兴。那些日子，全家人都会把盘子吃得精光，什么都不剩，”他说。每当讲起童年的故事，他总是面带微笑。而我一想到要碰那黏糊糊的青蛙，就觉得恶心。
paragraphs.14: 一天，父亲决定去试着抓些青蛙。他计划带我一起去体验我的第一次捕蛙之旅。他告诉我这会很有趣，从而说服了我去尝试。然而，母亲却反对他的想法。我告诉她，我现在的年龄已经和父亲当年开始抓青蛙时一样大了，她最终做出了让步。我告诉父亲我会带上几个蝴蝶网。“当你发现青蛙时，双手举起网，快速朝它罩下去，”父亲边说边用他的网做示范。“待在原地别动，直到我过去从网底下把它拿出来。”我爽快地答应了，因为我真的不想碰到青蛙。
paragraphs.22: 当夕阳落下最后一缕余晖，我们的捕猎正式开始了。我的心砰砰直跳。荒地上长满了带刺的含羞草。因为我们穿着拖鞋，那些讨人厌的杂草从侧面刺痛了我们的脚。穿着拖鞋走路很不舒服。荒地上还长着被称为茅草的高草。我们一边拨开茅草前进，一边小心翼翼防备不被它们锋利的边缘割伤。很快，我们发现用网并不容易。茅草太长了。当我们把网罩向青蛙时，厚厚的茅草弯曲并缓冲了网，在草和地面之间留出了足够的空间让青蛙逃跑。
paragraphs.30: 我们后来意识到，唯一的办法就是跟在它们后面跑，并试图用双手去抓住它们！我别无选择，只能克服恐惧。I紧张地蹲下身去抓一只，但无济于事。那些黏糊糊的家伙每次都从我手里滑走，逃进了地上的洞里。我很沮丧并想要放弃，但父亲鼓励我坚持下去。在尝试了很多次之后，我简直不敢相信自己终于抓到了一只。我高兴地欢呼起来，向父亲展示我的战利品。“往往是钥匙串上的最后一把钥匙打开了锁！”他说着，拍了拍我的肩膀。
paragraphs.38: 第二天午餐时，我们品尝了我们的劳动果实。在捕获的四只青蛙中，父亲说我抓的那只是最大的。当喝着青蛙粥时，我明白了一个道理：当事情不如意时，我们不应该放弃。
